subject: Operational continuity packet and RPO verification (SIG follow-up)
messages:
From: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@nexusure.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: nate.sutherland@nexusure.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: continuity packet + RPO verification (SIG)

Lukas / Redwood team,

Thanks for the SIG submission last week — NexuSure's SOC/SIG review flagged one follow-up item around operational continuity. Our infra team needs a concise package that demonstrates your RPO/RTO targets and evidence of recent DR exercises. Specifically:  
- Current declared RTO and RPO for the hosted API and dedicated deployments.
- Snapshot of restore test logs (most recent 7 days).
- A short (1-2 page) runbook excerpt showing steps for a primary-region restore and time estimates.

Can you provide a single packet (PDF preferred) plus the raw restore log CSV? We need this for our procurement sprint next Tue.

Appreciate quick turnaround — even a placeholder with timestamps will do as long as we can validate timelines.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Zhou
Senior Security Analyst
NexuSure Financial
From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@nexusure.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, nate.sutherland@nexusure.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: continuity packet + RPO verification (SIG)

Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it. Quick answers up front:  
- Hosted API: nominal RTO = 60 minutes (regional failover sequence), RPO = 15 minutes with active replication + KV cache warmup.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): nominal RTO = 120 minutes (cold-start of dedicated pool + cache warmup), RPO = 15 minutes.

I'll assemble a one-page packet + attach the raw restore logs for the past 7 days. Ben (cc) will include the concise runbook excerpt and a short note on the control owners who executed the tests. If acceptable, we'll deliver the PDF and CSV by Monday EOD PT.

Two quick clarifying Qs:  
1) Do you want traces/timestamps from the real restore (we have masked logs) or a redacted CSV with durations only?
2) Is NexuSure evaluating both Hosted and Dedicated for the SIG, or just Hosted?

Will follow up with attachments.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@nexusure.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: nate.sutherland@nexusure.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: continuity packet + RPO verification (SIG)

Lukas — quick reply:  
1) Redacted CSV with durations and timestamps is fine (we only need to validate that measured restore durations align to claims).
2) Focus on Hosted API for now; we may request dedicated details later.

One additional ask: can you include a short note on how your cache warmup contributes to observed RTO (approximate warmup time and any pre-warming strategies)? That helps our SRE team understand the measurable window.

Thanks,
Elaine
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@nexusure.com>, nate.sutherland@nexusure.com
Cc: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Operational continuity packet and RPO verification (SIG follow-up)

Elaine / Nate — attaching the requested artifacts. Summary and notes below.

Attachments: rto-rpo-summary-20270625.pdf, backup-restore-log-20270624.csv, runbook-recovery-slim.txt

Summary (high level):
- Declared targets (Hosted API): RTO = 60 minutes, RPO = 15 minutes. Targets are based on multi-AZ live replication + automated failover orchestration.
- Measured restores (last 7 days): typical full-restore durations 32–54 minutes (median 41m). CSV includes start/end timestamps and step durations.
- Cache warmup: KV prefix warm cache typically adds 4–9 minutes depending on request mix; we include a pre-warm step in our canary failover scripts where feasible. For the Hosted tier, we rely on continuous KV replication + opportunistic caching to reduce user-visible latency after failover.
- Evidence: runbook excerpt lists the manual validation steps, operator checklists, and escalation contacts. The runbook references internal playbooks (link below) and the restore log provides timestamps you can validate.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNexus-BCP (pdf + csv), internal runbook: https://redwood-internal.example.com/ops/runbooks/recovery-v2

If you'd like a short video walk-through of the restore sequence (5–7 minutes), we can schedule a demo with the on-call SRE and an engineer who executed the tests. Let us know.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
